<!-- bespoke-type-design-assessment-2026-10-14 -->
*This is Adler's Codex instance writing on Adler's behalf.*

### Bespoke type design assessment

This increment is assessed at **controversiality 6/10** and **additional error
prevention 4/10**. A new shared rig crate carries exact labels and ordinals,
anatomical fragments and string-based membership policies across fitting, export
and animation.

The assessment applies to inspected head
[`6a16b37f2818`](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/commit/6a16b37f2818d62e7a72d5b8c4645ec05f893265), against base `main` at
[`687983da6a90`](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/commit/687983da6a90da08884ff94a7aae6366a2edfb49). The PR head still matched at publication preflight. The
[epic score table](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/issues/726#issuecomment-6177690377)
defines the scales and compares the complete set.

Controversiality estimates review complexity, including supporting machinery; it
is not a defect count. Error prevention estimates additional API guarantees
relative to this increment's base. It is not a percentage, and per-type scores
are not additive.

#### Why these scores

**Complexity:** A new shared rig crate carries exact labels and ordinals,
anatomical fragments and string-based membership policies across fitting, export
and animation.

**Protected error classes:** Joint names, ordinals and anatomical parts are
distinct through many consumers, preventing wrong-kind arguments.

**Errors still possible:** Names admit arbitrary text, ordinals admit arbitrary
numbers, and substring/membership functions do not prove anatomical correctness
or existence in a specific rig.

| Type or owner | E /10 | Protection or retained guarantee | Limit |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `RigJointName` | 3 | Separates exact joint identity from other text and parts; centralized lookup can report absence. | Names admit arbitrary text, ordinals admit arbitrary numbers, and substring/membership functions do not prove anatomical correctness or existence in a specific rig. |
| `RigJointOrdinal` | 4 | Separates rig positions from names and unrelated numeric roles. | No bounds, rig identity, unique-name or generation/lifetime proof. |
| `RigJointPart` | 3 | Closed authored part vocabulary prevents arbitrary text from entering part-taking APIs. | The correct anatomical part or spelling must still be selected by authored data. |
| `RigSide` | 2 | Names left/right label roles. | Names admit arbitrary text, ordinals admit arbitrary numbers, and substring/membership functions do not prove anatomical correctness or existence in a specific rig. |
| `RigJointMembership` | 1 | Names included/excluded; does not certify successful anatomical analysis. | Names admit arbitrary text, ordinals admit arbitrary numbers, and substring/membership functions do not prove anatomical correctness or existence in a specific rig. |
| `RigJointLookupError` | 3 | Structured failures retain reason and native/joint context. | Names admit arbitrary text, ordinals admit arbitrary numbers, and substring/membership functions do not prove anatomical correctness or existence in a specific rig. |
| `ClothingError` | 3 | Structured failures retain reason and native/joint context. | Names admit arbitrary text, ordinals admit arbitrary numbers, and substring/membership functions do not prove anatomical correctness or existence in a specific rig. |
| `ForearmInputError` | 3 | Structured failures retain reason and native/joint context. | Names admit arbitrary text, ordinals admit arbitrary numbers, and substring/membership functions do not prove anatomical correctness or existence in a specific rig. |
| `ClothingPieceName` | 1 | Diagnostic role wrappers label already typed text/fixed arrays; no admission check. | Names admit arbitrary text, ordinals admit arbitrary numbers, and substring/membership functions do not prove anatomical correctness or existence in a specific rig. |
| `ClothingFaceContext` | 1 | Diagnostic role wrappers label already typed text/fixed arrays; no admission check. | Names admit arbitrary text, ordinals admit arbitrary numbers, and substring/membership functions do not prove anatomical correctness or existence in a specific rig. |
| `FrameLandmark` | 3 | Closed landmark roles reduce arbitrary label construction and wrong landmark lookup. | Names admit arbitrary text, ordinals admit arbitrary numbers, and substring/membership functions do not prove anatomical correctness or existence in a specific rig. |
| `TubeRig` | 2 | Names supported local rig choices. | Names admit arbitrary text, ordinals admit arbitrary numbers, and substring/membership functions do not prove anatomical correctness or existence in a specific rig. |
| `RigDefinition` | 0 | Moved cached records receive no new independent invariant credit. | Names admit arbitrary text, ordinals admit arbitrary numbers, and substring/membership functions do not prove anatomical correctness or existence in a specific rig. |
| `RigJoint` | 0 | Moved cached records receive no new independent invariant credit. | Names admit arbitrary text, ordinals admit arbitrary numbers, and substring/membership functions do not prove anatomical correctness or existence in a specific rig. |
| `JointSkinOwnership` | 2 | Named related fields reduce positional ownership/skin mistakes. | Names admit arbitrary text, ordinals admit arbitrary numbers, and substring/membership functions do not prove anatomical correctness or existence in a specific rig. |

#### Simpler design assessment

Keep identities thin; separate source-specific policies from generic identity.

**Keep:** Keep RigJointName, RigJointOrdinal, side/part roles where supplied to
APIs and typed lookup failures.

**Simpler alternative:** Move MHR naming, skin-family and garment substring
policy into their owning modules. If parts are used only for spellings and no
variant matching, a private data-backed JointPart vocabulary with named
constants can avoid enum/spelling duplication. Use ordinary predicates for local
tests, retaining membership enums where states cross APIs or native adapters.

**Utility retained:** Most utility: exact identity versus slot versus
anatomical-fragment separation and shared authoritative owners.

**Tradeoff and limits:** Moving policy improves responsibility boundaries more
than it reduces type count. Do not erase part/side roles or assume a thin
identity proves membership. A text-backed part must restrict construction to
preserve the authored vocabulary.

**Verification needed before adopting it:** First-duplicate lookup, exact
case/text/serialization, mirrored names, skin selection, fitting/export/native
words and shared-owner dependency placement.

#### Source and assessment limits

- [crates/fabelgeist-rig/src/lib.rs](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/6a16b37f2818d62e7a72d5b8c4645ec05f893265/crates/fabelgeist-rig/src/lib.rs)
- [crates/fabelgeist-rig/src/part.rs](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/6a16b37f2818d62e7a72d5b8c4645ec05f893265/crates/fabelgeist-rig/src/part.rs)

This is a static design assessment, not a completed correctness review or fresh
validation run. A moved type gets no independent new-invariant credit. Native
boundaries and pre-existing primitive distinctions are not counted twice. The
alternative, where proposed, has not been implemented or benchmarked; its
verification requirements are explicit. No new merge condition or ownership
assignment is implied.

*This is Bruno's Codex instance writing on Bruno's behalf.*

@halbe, I adopted the ownership recommendation from your
[design assessment](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/pull/774#issuecomment-6177719521).

The shared rig crate retains exact joint names, ordinals, side/part roles and
lookup errors. Momentum Human Rig naming and mirroring live in a lightweight
profile module; garment twist selection belongs to clothing, and animation
classification belongs to animation admission. The shared crate does not need
the tensor runtime for those naming conventions.

The garment-ordering predicate returns `bool`. Membership enums remain where
the result crosses fitting APIs or becomes a shader word. Rig-order collections
accept ordinals directly, with checked access when membership is unproven.
Neither an ordinal nor a name proves membership in a particular rig, and exact
name lookup still preserves the first duplicate.

Direct authored joint names now use typed constants. The separate fragment
vocabulary, `RigJointPart`, remains a closed enum with strum-backed spellings
rather than private text-backed constants. Its construction remains restricted
without a handwritten spelling match. Ordinary conversions and formatting use
derives where their contracts allow it.

Independent Code, Rule and Comment Review passed static inspection of the
review response. [Hosted validation](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/actions/runs/39156838818) passed on
`ac20b9205127f71d1e114125872502bd8a1e9491`,
including the retained rig, fitting and animation
selections. The relevant existing growth allowances were reduced using the
verified source snapshot. No new tests were added during this review response,
and no gates or allowances were relaxed.

This verifies the selected paths, not complete creator generation, production
assets, direct engine-name/socket behavior or visual acceptance. Direct FBX
name/duration admission, report serialization and audio-seed behavior also lack
dedicated existing behavioral coverage. The PR body records these limits and
the remaining height, animated-track and FBX graph-identity follow-ups.

Following up on the [blend-weight review thread](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/pull/774#discussion_r4306847772).

*Bruno’s Codex instance, writing on Bruno’s behalf.*

Please propagate the checked blend-weight type further upstream in #774.
`PoseSample.weight` in `adventuresim-tactical-core::animation::evaluation`
is still `f32`, so the resolver and inverse-kinematics consumers repeatedly
admit the same quantity with `BlendWeight::from_factor`.

Place the canonical owner in the lowest shared animation module and carry
it through `PoseSample`, the evaluation producers, resolver inputs and
accumulation. Admit raw values at authored literals, deserialization and
actual framework boundaries. Weight-producing arithmetic should preserve
the checked type and reject overflow before publishing replacement values.

Preserve the established contract: finite, nonnegative, zero allowed, and
contributions above one allowed. Please complete this producer-to-consumer
propagation in this PR and validate it with the existing hosted checks.

Additional producer scope from the architectural review:

- [`PoseSampling::Cycle.phase`](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/ac20b9205127f71d1e114125872502bd8a1e9491/crates/adventuresim-tactical-core/src/animation/evaluation.rs#L15)
  has an existing exact quantity owner, `CyclePhase`. Move the canonical
  owner into shared animation core and carry it from the evaluation
  producer to the resolver, preserving finite signed/unwrapped cycles.
- `PoseSample.mirror_lower_body` carries the original/mirrored choice.
  Reuse the existing `ClipMirror` meaning through a canonical shared owner
  instead of keeping an internal Boolean that the client readmits later.
  Keep any required Boolean wire encoding at the serialization adapter.
- Do not use `CyclePhase` as a generic validator for action progress,
  pose-extrapolation coordinates or tangent magnitudes. Their different
  contracts need their own complete producer-to-consumer migrations.

The [four-field continuation migration](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/pull/774#issuecomment-6255298111)
remains explicitly deferred to a separate PR. That deferral does not cover
the current upstream `BlendWeight` request or reuse of the matching cyclic
phase and mirror-choice owners above. Coordinate zero-weight plan topology
and numerical presence with [#944](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/pull/944).

Typed-error migration remains a separate PR; reuse existing error owners
for this work rather than expanding the database-facing error migration.

*Bruno’s Codex instance, writing on Bruno’s behalf.*

**Defer these four continuation parameters to a separate PR.** This covers
`ContinuationSpan.start_coordinate`, `incoming_tangent`, `ready_phase` and
`progress` in
`crates/adventuresim-tactical-client/src/animation/continuation.rs`.

The follow-up should define canonical checked types in the shared
attack-animation owner and preserve these distinct contracts:

- Pose coordinate: finite, with intentional drawback and overshoot outside
  `[0, 1]` retained.
- Incoming tangent: finite and nonnegative.
- Ready phase: finite and strictly between `0` and `0.5`.
- Action progress: finite and within `[0, 1]`, without wrapping.

Carry them through `QueuedAttack` / `AttackSequence`,
`PoseSampling::ContinuationSpan`, `ContinuationSpan`,
`ContinuationTransition` and spline evaluation as one complete migration.
Keep the current finite-value checks and existing behavior in place until
that follow-up lands; `CyclePhase` is not a matching owner for all four.

This deferral is limited to these continuation parameters. The separately
requested upstream `BlendWeight` propagation and `LocomotionHeightState`
quantity typing remain current work for #774.

*Bruno’s Codex instance, writing on Bruno’s behalf.*

Additional review findings against `ac20b9205127f71d1e114125872502bd8a1e9491`:

1. **Coordinate the epsilon and zero-weight policies with [#944](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/pull/944).**
   [`semantic_foot_ik_weights`](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/ac20b9205127f71d1e114125872502bd8a1e9491/crates/adventuresim-tactical-client/src/animation/mod.rs#L734)
   still returns zero when the total is below `f32::EPSILON`. A valid tiny
   positive idle contribution therefore produces zero IK influence, despite
   the new policy that every positive contribution counts. #944 already
   targets this calculation. Apply its numerical-comparison policy: exact
   presence checks for presence, checked normalization, and explicit
   quantity-specific error bounds where approximation is actually needed.
   Do not replace machine epsilon with another arbitrary universal cutoff.

   There is also a behavior overlap to reconcile: #944 retains declared
   zero-weight `PoseSampling::Span` endpoints to preserve playback-plan
   topology while skipping their sampling contributions. #774 currently
   [returns early for zero weight](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/ac20b9205127f71d1e114125872502bd8a1e9491/crates/adventuresim-tactical-client/src/animation/weighted.rs#L43).
   Carrying checked weights upstream must preserve that distinction between
   declared topology and an absent numerical contribution.

2. **Specify and enforce the measurement-blend range.**
   [`phase_drift_measurement_blend`](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/ac20b9205127f71d1e114125872502bd8a1e9491/crates/adventuresim-tactical-core/src/combat_config/playback.rs#L14)
   currently accepts any finite nonnegative value. It is used in
   `remaining += (measurement - remaining) * blend`; values above one
   extrapolate, and sufficiently large accepted values can overflow the
   retained accumulator. Establish the intended interpolation contract and
   enforce it at configuration admission. The broader bespoke-type
   migration can remain separate from correcting this range.

3. **Make cached rig classification consistent by construction.**
   [`AuthoredRigJoint`](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/ac20b9205127f71d1e114125872502bd8a1e9491/crates/adventuresim-tactical-client/src/animation/rig_identity.rs#L8)
   exposes its name separately from cached body-region and bone-role
   fields. A name update need not recompute the classifications. Keep the
   fields private and provide read-only access or one coordinated update
   operation. This is an encapsulation gap; no current mutation causing a
   runtime failure has been established.

4. **Avoid making catalogue classification depend on a memory address.**
   [`RuntimeClothingRole::from`](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/ac20b9205127f71d1e114125872502bd8a1e9491/crates/adventuresim-character-creator/src/runtime_equipment.rs#L62)
   recognizes the belt using `std::ptr::eq`. An equivalent cloned item
   definition would classify differently. Current callers supply canonical
   catalogue references, so this is a latent API-contract weakness rather
   than an observed failure. Express the canonical-handle requirement in
   the input type, or classify through explicit catalogue-owned data.

5. **Remaining production `.expect()` calls violate the repository rule.**
   [Clothing hash serialization](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/ac20b9205127f71d1e114125872502bd8a1e9491/crates/adventuresim-character-creator/src/runtime_equipment/clothing.rs#L81)
   can propagate its error through the existing result.
   [Catalogue pose construction](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/ac20b9205127f71d1e114125872502bd8a1e9491/crates/adventuresim-tactical-client/src/animation/catalog.rs#L174)
   should use the existing `SemanticPose` variants directly instead of
   parsing known strings and calling `.expect()`.
   The governing [Rust guide](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/ac20b9205127f71d1e114125872502bd8a1e9491/crates/AGENTS.md#L126)
   prohibits `unwrap` and `expect` outside tests.

Clarifications on the other review comments:

- `item_catalog.rs:379` is inside `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`; its
  `.unwrap()` is permitted by that rule.
- Checked deserialization can use derived `Deserialize` with
  `#[serde(try_from = "f32")]` and a validated `TryFrom<f32>`.
  An ordinary transparent derive would bypass admission. The existing
  [`MapZoomRatio`](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/ac20b9205127f71d1e114125872502bd8a1e9491/crates/adventuresim-tactical-core/src/regional_map.rs#L23)
  demonstrates the checked-derive pattern.
- Finite vector components do not guarantee a finite squared length or
  finite subsequent arithmetic. Preserve overflow checks in checked
  operations; constructor validation alone does not justify removing them.

*Bruno’s Codex instance, writing on Bruno’s behalf.*

**Keep bounded animation influence distinct from additive blend weight.**

[`whole_body_mirror`](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/ac20b9205127f71d1e114125872502bd8a1e9491/crates/adventuresim-tactical-client/src/animation/mod.rs#L145)
currently uses `BlendWeight`, which correctly permits values above one.
The per-foot inverse-kinematics influences are carried as an unlabelled
`Vec2`. Both results have finite `[0, 1]` contracts, unlike accumulated
contributions.

Please establish one canonical checked bounded-influence owner and use a
named left/right influence record where both feet travel together. Carry
these values through their producers, playback state, pose buffering and
inverse-kinematics consumers; expose native scalars/vectors at the actual
numerical kernels. Keep `BlendWeight` for additive contributions, without
restricting its range.

The braking-lean scale already has a current review request. Its semantic
role should remain clear even if a common bounded numeric leaf is reused.
Do not conflate a fractional reflection influence with the binary
original/mirrored clip selection.

This bounded-influence family can be implemented as its own complete,
focused follow-up increment rather than mixed into the separately
requested upstream contribution migration. Preserve existing clamping
policy at the owning admission point; do not silently introduce wrapping
or change accepted boundary behavior. Reuse existing error owners and
existing hosted checks; structured-error migration stays separate.

*Bruno’s Codex instance, writing on Bruno’s behalf.*

**Configuration typing must preserve relationships as well as leaf values.**

For the follow-up configuration migration, please close these contracts in
[`AnimationLandingConfig`](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/ac20b9205127f71d1e114125872502bd8a1e9491/crates/adventuresim-tactical-core/src/combat_config/landing.rs#L9),
[`LandingProfile`](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/ac20b9205127f71d1e114125872502bd8a1e9491/crates/adventuresim-tactical-core/src/animation/locomotion.rs#L31)
and
[`AnimationPlaybackConfig`](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/ac20b9205127f71d1e114125872502bd8a1e9491/crates/adventuresim-tactical-core/src/combat_config/playback.rs#L8):

- Landing recovery is strictly positive. `AnimationElapsed` intentionally
  accepts zero for other operations, so that leaf alone cannot establish
  the landing-recovery guarantee.
- Minimum and maximum compression must be nonnegative, permit zero, and
  satisfy minimum <= maximum.
- Locomotion thresholds must remain ordered:
  deactivation <= initial <= activation.

Use checked construction/deserialization and controlled field access so
callers cannot invalidate a previously checked record by assigning public
fields independently. Carry the guarantees into the runtime profile;
do not validate YAML and then project into a freely constructible record
that loses the relationships.

Reuse canonical leaves where their contracts match. For example,
`LandingImpactSpeed` fits the minimum-impact threshold and `SignedLength`
fits the visual Y offset. `PositiveLength` rejects zero, so it is not a
drop-in replacement for zero-permitting compression. Define only the
missing distinctions. Keep the canonical YAML default owner and existing
scalar wire encodings.

This records the broader configuration follow-up; it does not remove the
existing current-PR request to use `SignedLength`, or the separately
[reported measurement-blend range correction](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/pull/774#issuecomment-6255360371).
Typed errors are deliberately deferred to a separate PR: retain existing
error owners here rather than expanding that migration.

*Bruno’s Codex instance, writing on Bruno’s behalf.*

**Follow-up: close the rig aggregate contract before adding more elaborate ordinals.**

[`RigJointTable<T>`](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/ac20b9205127f71d1e114125872502bd8a1e9491/crates/fabelgeist-rig/src/table.rs#L7)
correctly distinguishes a joint slot from unrelated integer categories.
Its documented limit remains important: a `RigJointOrdinal` does not
prove membership in a particular rig, and separately constructed tables
do not establish matching lengths or order.

Please make the next rig-family increment a validated aggregate built
from one authoritative rig ordering, pairing the names, parent links,
transforms and associated joint columns that must agree. Establish shape
and parent-membership/order requirements at admission, and control later
mutation so those guarantees survive. Preserve each rig/source's existing
order rather than imposing a universal reordering. Check or explicitly
establish receiving-rig membership when ordinals cross an unproven
boundary.

Retain checked access for unproven ordinals and direct typed indexing
where construction or traversal establishes validity. The current public
ordinal must not be treated as a membership certificate. Lifetime-branded
indices are optional; a focused owning aggregate may be sufficient.

Keep open exact joint names, first-duplicate lookup behavior, source
naming profiles and clothing/animation policies separate as they are now.
This should be one complete follow-up PR with its actual producers and
consumers, rather than a second independently defined joint-index family.
It does not require the deliberately deferred typed-error migration.

*Bruno's Codex instance, writing on Bruno's behalf.*

Reviewing `f0ba1326`, [`crates/adventuresim-tactical-client/src/animation/mod.rs:117`](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/f0ba1326179fae1c345f83aa31ded5529ee5cd87/crates/adventuresim-tactical-client/src/animation/mod.rs#L117-L118).

**Carry CalibrationMotion through the whole calibration cache.** The producer in
`stride_calibration::calibrate` already iterates `CalibrationMotion`, but both
caches retain `MotionId`; `clear_motion` then recovers the four roles through
name comparisons, while `sample_phase` independently spells out walk/run IDs.
Please move the existing enum to a shared owner, key these calibration caches
by that enum, and use an explicit pose-to-calibration-role mapping for sampling.
Convert the role to `MotionId` when looking up the runtime animation asset.
This closes the producer/cache/consumer family and makes adding a role subject
to exhaustive matching. Keep the general motion identity open for other assets.
This is a migration-completeness gap rather than a demonstrated new runtime
failure. See the [producer-propagation rule](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/f0ba1326179fae1c345f83aa31ded5529ee5cd87/crates/AGENTS.md#L36-L42).

Source inspection only; no tests were run or added.

*Bruno's Codex instance, writing on Bruno's behalf.*

Reviewing `f0ba1326`, [`crates/adventuresim-tactical-client/src/animation_viewer/capture.rs:358`](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/f0ba1326179fae1c345f83aa31ded5529ee5cd87/crates/adventuresim-tactical-client/src/animation_viewer/capture.rs#L358-L362).

**Carry scenario policy through execution and validation.** `PlannedFrame`
already carries `ScenarioMetadata`, but this path extracts its label to recover
body state and required motion, compares the returned motion text, then
reconstructs `MotionId`. Elsewhere capture inspects label prefixes/suffixes for
impact, aim and attack behavior; dive direction is independently reconstructed
in `dive_impact_scenario_with_aim` and `transition_for_scenario`. Report metrics
and validation also choose acceptance thresholds from label fragments. Please
admit these choices once into typed scenario payloads, reusing `ScenarioKind`,
`BodyState`, `PostureTransitionKind`, `DiveDirection` and `MotionId`, and retain
the relevant policy through capture and report analysis. Labels should serve
selection and output; changing one should not silently change scenario behavior
or its acceptance policy. Preserve existing labels, unknown-label behavior and
threshold values. This is the remaining propagation beyond terrain-policy
admission, following the [producer-propagation rule](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/f0ba1326179fae1c345f83aa31ded5529ee5cd87/crates/AGENTS.md#L36-L42).

Source inspection only; no tests were run or added.

*Bruno's Codex instance, writing on Bruno's behalf.*

Reviewing `f0ba1326`, [`crates/adventuresim-tactical-client/src/animation_viewer/capture.rs:156`](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/f0ba1326179fae1c345f83aa31ded5529ee5cd87/crates/adventuresim-tactical-client/src/animation_viewer/capture.rs#L156).

**Retain bone roles through capture analysis.** `collect_bones` starts with
`HumanoidBone.role: BoneRole`, but `tracked_bone` immediately converts it to a
string key retained here and in `FrameSample.bones`. The values are still used
for internal analysis: `jitter_frames` identifies the pelvis by text and
`parent_bone(&str)` matches the labels again to reconstruct the reporting
hierarchy. A label change therefore requires synchronized changes to analysis
logic. Please keep the existing `BoneRole` as the collection key through
capture, repeated-evaluation checks and metrics/jitter analysis, express the
captured-parent relation over that role, and emit the current label spellings
at report serialization. That relation belongs to the reduced reporting
hierarchy, not to the full authored skeleton. Existing JSON keys and numerical
behavior can remain intact. This retained migration gap follows the
[producer-propagation rule](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/f0ba1326179fae1c345f83aa31ded5529ee5cd87/crates/AGENTS.md#L36-L42).

Source inspection only; no tests were run or added.

*Bruno's Codex instance, writing on Bruno's behalf.*

Please simplify the Boolean wire adapters for these three enums. Keep the two small explicit `From` mappings and derive `Serialize`/`Deserialize` through them, rather than handwriting the generic serializer/deserializer implementations:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(from = "bool", into = "bool")]
pub enum ClipMirror {
    Original,
    Mirrored,
}
```

The derives delegate to `From<bool> for T` and `From<T> for bool`; they do not infer which variant means `true`.

- **[ClipMirror](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/8231944d8161f75898448898f6ee854233dac938/crates/adventuresim-tactical-core/src/animation/sample_values.rs#L174):** Restore the previous derive-through-conversions pattern: `true` maps to `Mirrored`, `false` to `Original`, and the inverse conversion produces the same Boolean wire value.
